title: AI’s Historical Present: It’s Plagiarism, Right?
author: Tim Moon
summary: Moon, a former school leader, recounts the August 2023 case when three juniors were suspected of using ChatGPT on a summer reading essay. His school's plagiarism policy, which gave a zero, did not fit a tool that was both plagiarizer and plagiarized. He used a weekend to learn about the technology and decided he could not punish what he could not prove, so he apologised to the parents, imposed a moratorium on AI use and wrote a new policy over a month. The policy left permission to teachers, who had to set clear expectations and report only demonstrable violations. He closes arguing that AI, used with restraint, is a generational tool whose main K-12 benefit is relieving teachers of drudgery. The piece is a first-person case study in school AI policy.
points: An integrity policy written for copying did not cover a generative tool, so punishing students would have meant acting without proof.
The school paused AI use, apologised to parents and wrote a policy rather than enforcing an unfit rule.
The resulting policy delegated permission to teachers, with clear expectations and only demonstrable violations reported.
Moon argues the largest K-12 payoff of AI is relieving teachers of mechanical drudgery.
quotes: In this case, ChatGPT was both the plagiarizer and the plagiarized. The culprit, and the victim.

Rather than punish students for something we could not adequately prove, I decided to take a timeout and use this incident as an opportunity to develop a policy that would be effective and enforceable for the future.
I was not going to punish someone unless I was sure they were guilty.
The policy took about a month to develop. It ultimately left the decision to allow or disallow the use of AI up to the teacher.
I am convinced today that, used with proper restraints, AI provides a generational learning tool for students and teachers.

Used properly, AI can relieve much of the burdensome mechanical drudgery that currently befalls so many of our teachers, and perhaps regenerate the love for learning and teaching that drew them to be teachers in the first place.
One comment by a programmer had particular significance. He compared using ChatGPT to write to using a calculator for math.
